1.1 This manual defines the mandatory maintenance schedules and procedures for all club assets, including the North Pavilion (N.Pav), South Pavilion, main and secondary pitches, floodlighting, and associated grounds equipment.

1.2 It applies to all facilities staff, groundskeepers, volunteers undertaking maintenance tasks, and contractors working on behalf of the club.

1.3 Where a specific asset is not covered in this manual, the Facilities Lead shall be consulted before any maintenance work is undertaken.

1.4 Nothing in this manual overrides statutory obligations, manufacturer instructions, or insurance requirements.

2. General Responsibilities

2.1 The ADSC Committee has overall responsibility for the adoption and review of this manual. Day-to-day oversight is delegated to the Facilities Lead (M.C.).

2.2 The Grounds Manager (J. Whitfield) is responsible for pitch maintenance and grounds equipment.

2.3 Volunteers must not undertake any task for which they have not received training. A record of volunteer training is held in the club office.

2.4 Any defect or hazard noted during routine checks must be reported to the Facilities Lead within 24 hours, or immediately if it poses a safety risk.

2.5 Contractors must sign in at the club office and be issued with a site safety briefing before commencing work.

3. North Pavilion (N.Pav)

3.1 Daily Opening Checklist (performed by duty staff or trained volunteer)

ADSC Maintenance Manual 2019 adopted_date 2019-04-01 date. Record status: historical.

- Unlock main entrance and check for signs of forced entry.
- Check that all interior lights are functional; replace any faulty bulbs.
- Verify that the heating system is operating at the set temperature (normally 18°C in winter, 15°C in summer).
- Inspect the kitchen area for cleanliness and check that the refrigerator is at the correct temperature.
- Ensure that all fire exits are clear and accessible.
- Check that the first aid kit is fully stocked and items are within their expiry dates.
- Sign the daily log sheet in the office.

3.2 Weekly Inspection (every Monday)

- Test all electrical sockets using a portable appliance tester (PAT) for club-owned equipment.
- Inspect the roof for leaks or damage, particularly after heavy rain or storms.
- Check that all window locks are functional.
- Clean the gutters if there is visible debris.
- Report any issues to the Facilities Lead.

3.3 Monthly Boiler Check (first Tuesday of the month)

- Check the boiler pressure gauge (should read between 1.0 and 1.5 bar when cold).
- Bleed radiators if necessary to remove trapped air.
- Record the boiler pressure and any adjustments made in the boiler log book.
- Check that the condensate pipe is clear and free of ice during winter months.

3.4 Quarterly Deep Clean (March, June, September, December)

- Arrange for a professional cleaning contractor to carry out a full deep clean of the pavilion, including kitchen extraction unit, changing rooms, and public areas.
- Ensure that the cleaning contractor holds the relevant insurance and follows club safeguarding policies.

3.5 Annual Structural Inspection (April)

- A qualified building surveyor shall inspect the pavilion structure, including foundations, roof, and external walls.
- The surveyor shall provide a written report to the Facilities Lead, with any recommended works categorised by priority (urgent, routine, or cosmetic).

4. South Pavilion

4.1 The South Pavilion is used primarily for storage and occasional match-day refreshments. It is subject to the same daily, weekly, and monthly checks as the North Pavilion, except where noted below.

4.2 The South Pavilion does not have a fixed heating system. Portable heaters may be used during match days, provided they are PAT tested and placed clear of flammable materials.
5. Grounds Maintenance

5.1 General

The club grounds comprise the main playing field (north), the training area (south-west), the practice nets, and the surrounding perimeter paths. Grounds staff shall carry out the tasks below in addition to the daily litter pick described in Section 2.

5.2 Weekly Grounds Inspection (every Friday)

- Walk the full perimeter and check fencing for damage, gaps, or loose posts.
- Inspect the playing surface for divots, bare patches, or standing water.
- Check the practice nets for tears and ensure the frames are secure.
- Clear any debris from the drainage channels around the main field.
- Record the condition of the grounds in the weekly log sheet, noting any areas that require attention.

5.3 Mowing Schedule

The main playing field shall be mown twice per week during the growing season (April to October) and once per week during the remainder of the year, weather permitting. The training area shall be mown once per week during the growing season. Mowing shall not take place when the ground is waterlogged or during periods of frost.

5.4 Fertiliser and Top Dressing

- Fertiliser shall be applied to the main playing field in early April and again in early September, using a product approved by the Facilities Lead.
- Top dressing shall be carried out in October, at a rate of approximately 5 tonnes per pitch, to level the surface and encourage root growth.
- All application dates and product names shall be recorded in the Grounds Log Book.

5.5 Aeration

- The main playing field shall be hollow-tine aerated in March and September.
- The training area shall be spiked in May and July.
- Aeration shall be carried out when the soil is moist but not saturated.

5.6 Perimeter Paths

- Perimeter paths shall be swept weekly and any weeds treated with an approved herbicide.
- Loose or broken paving slabs shall be reported to the Facilities Lead and made safe with hazard tape until repaired.

5.7 Trees and Hedges

- Hedges shall be trimmed in August, after the nesting season.
- Trees shall be inspected annually in autumn for dead or dangerous branches. Any such branches shall be removed by a qualified contractor.
- Fallen leaves shall be cleared from paths and the playing surface as required during autumn.

6. Water Quality Testing

6.1 The club has two water features: the ornamental pond near the North Pavilion and the drinking water fountain by the main entrance. The pond is not used for swimming or any other recreational purpose.

6.2 Ornamental Pond

- The pond water shall be tested weekly between April and September, and monthly from October to March.
- The test shall measure pH, ammonia, nitrite, and nitrate levels.
- The results shall be recorded in the Water Quality Log, noting the date, time, and the initials of the person carrying out the test.
- If the pH falls outside the range 6.5 to 8.5, or if ammonia or nitrite levels are above 0.5 mg/l, the Facilities Lead shall be notified and a partial water change shall be carried out.
- The pond pump and filter shall be checked monthly and cleaned as necessary.

6.3 Drinking Water Fountain

- The drinking water fountain shall be inspected weekly for leaks, blockages, and general cleanliness.
- The filter shall be replaced every six months, or sooner if the flow rate reduces noticeably.
- A water sample shall be sent to a UKAS-accredited laboratory annually in June, for microbiological analysis.
- The laboratory certificate shall be filed in the Water Quality Log.

6.4 Emergency Water Supply

In the event of a mains water failure, the club has an emergency water butt located behind the South Pavilion. This supply is for cleaning purposes only and is not suitable for drinking. The butt shall be emptied and cleaned annually in March, and the tap checked for operation.

**1. INTRODUCTION AND SCOPE**

1.1 This manual sets out the maintenance standards for the ADSC site, including the Clubhouse, North Pavilion (N.Pav), South Pavilion (S.Pav), the main pitch, training area, and the floodlighting masts.

1.2 The manual is intended for use by facilities staff, groundskeepers, and trained volunteers. Contractors must also be made aware of relevant sections before starting work.

1.3 Where a procedure refers to a specific form or log, the current version of that form is held in the ring binder on the Clubhouse noticeboard and in the digital folder `ADSC/Maintenance/2023`.

1.4 The Clubhouse heating system and the pavilion heating systems are gas-fired. Any work on gas appliances must only be carried out by a Gas Safe registered engineer. This is not a delegation of that duty.

---

**2. GENERAL RESPONSIBILITIES**

2.1 The Facilities Sub-committee is responsible for the overall coordination of maintenance, for keeping this manual up to date, and for arranging annual inspections by external specialists.

ADSC Maintenance Manual 2023 adopted_date 2023-06-15 date. Record status: current.

2.2 The Head Groundskeeper (currently R. Singh) is responsible for the pitch, training area, and all grounds equipment.

2.3 The Clubhouse Manager (currently P. Doyle) is responsible for the Clubhouse fabric, heating, and daily checks.

2.4 Volunteers undertaking tasks under this manual must have read and signed the relevant task sheet. A volunteer must never undertake a task they are not confident to perform; they should stop and report to the Head Groundskeeper or Clubhouse Manager.

2.5 Any defect that poses an immediate safety risk must be reported to the Clubhouse Manager or Head Groundskeeper immediately. If neither is available, follow the Out-of-Hours Procedure in Section 11.

2.6 **Reporting defects:** Log all defects in the Defect Log (paper copy on noticeboard, or digital copy in the shared drive). Include date, time, location, description, and your name. Do not attempt repairs outside your competence.

---

**3. DAILY OPENING AND CLOSING CHECKS (CLUBHOUSE AND PAVILIONS)**

3.1 These checks are to be carried out by the duty staff member or trained volunteer. The completed checklist must be signed and dated, and filed in the weekly folder.

3.2 **Opening Checks (Clubhouse)**

- Unlock main door and set intruder alarm to "part arm" if applicable.
- Check for overnight water leaks: inspect under sinks, behind toilets, and around the boiler cupboard. Report any dampness or pooling immediately.
- Check boiler pressure gauge reads between 1.0 and 1.5 bar when cold. If below 1.0 bar, top up using the filling loop (see section 5.4).
- Check that the heating programmer is set for the correct day and time. Reset if the power was interrupted overnight.
- Check that all emergency exit routes are clear and that the emergency lighting test switch is in the normal position.
- Check that the fridge/freezer in the kitchen is running and the internal temperature is below 5°C.

3.3 **Opening Checks (Pavilions)** – N.Pav and S.Pav

- Unlock and check for signs of forced entry or vandalism.
- Check that the water stopcock is in the open position (only close for winterisation or emergency).
- Check that the toilet flush operates and there is no continuous running water.
- Check that the heater timer is set correctly, if the heater is in use.
**4. GROUNDS MAINTENANCE**

4.1 The Head Groundskeeper is responsible for the overall condition of the playing surfaces, surrounds, and access paths. Daily and weekly tasks are set out below. Seasonal tasks (e.g. end-of-season renovation) are planned separately and communicated by notice on the Grounds Office door and by email.

4.2 **Daily Grounds Checks (playing season, March–October)**

- Walk the perimeter of each pitch before play. Look for glass, litter, dog fouling, or damage to fencing. Remove any debris and log the action in the Grounds Log.
- Check goalposts are secure and padding is in place for all junior matches. Report any loose fixings to the Head Groundskeeper.
- Check that the corner flags are present and not damaged.
- Inspect the run-off areas and spectator lines for trip hazards, especially where the ground has been wet.

4.3 **Weekly Pitch Inspection**

- Carry out a full inspection of each pitch, including the outfield areas. Use the Pitch Inspection Record (Form G-2) and note the following:
  - Grass length (measured with the sward stick, recorded in mm).
  - Any bare patches, divots, or worm casts that need attention.
  - Drainage issues: standing water, soft spots, or silt build-up.
  - Condition of the pitch surrounds, including any damage to the mower access gate.
- The completed form must be handed to the Head Groundskeeper by Friday 12:00. The Head Groundskeeper will decide whether any remedial work is required and will allocate the work accordingly.

4.4 **Mowing**

- Mowing heights are set by the Head Groundskeeper and vary by season. The current settings are displayed on the mower shed noticeboard.
- Do not mow when the grass is wet unless specifically instructed. When mowing, use the agreed pattern (alternate direction each cut) to avoid compaction.
- After mowing, check the underside of the mower for build-up of grass and clean if necessary.
- Report any unusual vibration or cutting irregularities to the Head Groundskeeper before the next use.

4.5 **Fertiliser and Top Dressing**

- Only the Head Groundskeeper or a trained groundsperson may apply fertiliser, top dressing, or other soil amendments.
- All applications must be recorded on the Chemical/Amendment Log (Form G-4), including product name, quantity, area treated, and weather conditions.
- Keep all product safety data sheets in the Grounds Office. The current list of approved products is available from the Clubhouse Manager.

4.6 **Irrigation**

- The automatic irrigation system (N.Pav and S.Pav pitches) is to be tested each Monday morning during the playing season. Check for leaks, blocked heads, and correct timer settings.
- If the system is used manually, the person operating it must remain on site until the cycle is complete.
- Any faults with the irrigation controller should be reported to the Head Groundskeeper and logged in the Defect Log.

---

**5. BOILER AND HEATING SYSTEMS**

5.1 These procedures apply to the clubhouse boiler and the heating systems in N.Pav and S.Pav. Only the Clubhouse Manager or a nominated contractor may carry out work on the boilers themselves. Volunteers must not remove any boiler casing or attempt repairs.

5.2 **Monthly Boiler Check (Clubhouse)**

- Check the pressure gauge. The normal cold reading is between 1.0 and 1.5 bar. If the reading is below 1.0 bar, top up using the filling loop (see 5.4).
- Check that the condensate pipe is not blocked or leaking.
- Check the flue terminal outside for obstructions (e.g. bird nests or debris).
- Listen for unusual noises (kettling, banging) and note any smells of gas or combustion. If gas is smelled, follow the emergency procedure in Section 11.
- Record the check on the Boiler Check Sheet (Form H-2) and file it in the monthly folder.

1.1 This manual defines the mandatory maintenance schedules and procedures for all club assets, including the North Pavilion (N.Pav), South Pavilion, main and secondary pitches, floodlighting, and associated grounds equipment.

1.2 It applies to all facilities staff, groundskeepers, volunteers undertaking maintenance tasks, and contractors working on behalf of the club.

1.3 Where a specific asset is not covered in this manual, the Facilities Lead shall be consulted before any maintenance work is undertaken.

1.4 Nothing in this manual overrides statutory obligations, manufacturer instructions, or insurance requirements.

2. General Responsibilities

2.1 The ADSC Committee has overall responsibility for the adoption and review of this manual. Day-to-day oversight is delegated to the Facilities Lead (M.C.).

2.2 The Grounds Manager (J. Whitfield) is responsible for pitch maintenance and grounds equipment.

2.3 Volunteers must not undertake any task for which they have not received training. A record of volunteer training is held in the club office.

2.4 Any defect or hazard noted during routine checks must be reported to the Facilities Lead within 24 hours, or immediately if it poses a safety risk.

2.5 Contractors must sign in at the club office and be issued with a site safety briefing before commencing work.

3. North Pavilion (N.Pav)

3.1 Daily Opening Checklist (performed by duty staff or trained volunteer)

ADSC Maintenance Manual 2019 adopted_date 2019-04-01 date. Record status: historical.

- Unlock main entrance and check for signs of forced entry.
- Check that all interior lights are functional; replace any faulty bulbs.
- Verify that the heating system is operating at the set temperature (normally 18°C in winter, 15°C in summer).
- Inspect the kitchen area for cleanliness and check that the refrigerator is at the correct temperature.
- Ensure that all fire exits are clear and accessible.
- Check that the first aid kit is fully stocked and items are within their expiry dates.
- Sign the daily log sheet in the office.

3.2 Weekly Inspection (every Monday)

- Test all electrical sockets using a portable appliance tester (PAT) for club-owned equipment.
- Inspect the roof for leaks or damage, particularly after heavy rain or storms.
- Check that all window locks are functional.
- Clean the gutters if there is visible debris.
- Report any issues to the Facilities Lead.

3.3 Monthly Boiler Check (first Tuesday of the month)

- Check the boiler pressure gauge (should read between 1.0 and 1.5 bar when cold).
- Bleed radiators if necessary to remove trapped air.
- Record the boiler pressure and any adjustments made in the boiler log book.
- Check that the condensate pipe is clear and free of ice during winter months.

3.4 Quarterly Deep Clean (March, June, September, December)

- Arrange for a professional cleaning contractor to carry out a full deep clean of the pavilion, including kitchen extraction unit, changing rooms, and public areas.
- Ensure that the cleaning contractor holds the relevant insurance and follows club safeguarding policies.

3.5 Annual Structural Inspection (April)

- A qualified building surveyor shall inspect the pavilion structure, including foundations, roof, and external walls.
- The surveyor shall provide a written report to the Facilities Lead, with any recommended works categorised by priority (urgent, routine, or cosmetic).

4. South Pavilion

4.1 The South Pavilion is used primarily for storage and occasional match-day refreshments. It is subject to the same daily, weekly, and monthly checks as the North Pavilion, except where noted below.

4.2 The South Pavilion does not have a fixed heating system. Portable heaters may be used during match days, provided they are PAT tested and placed clear of flammable materials.

5. Grounds Maintenance

5.1 General

The club grounds comprise the main playing field (north), the training area (south-west), the practice nets, and the surrounding perimeter paths. Grounds staff shall carry out the tasks below in addition to the daily litter pick described in Section 2.

5.2 Weekly Grounds Inspection (every Friday)

- Walk the full perimeter and check fencing for damage, gaps, or loose posts.
- Inspect the playing surface for divots, bare patches, or standing water.
- Check the practice nets for tears and ensure the frames are secure.
- Clear any debris from the drainage channels around the main field.
- Record the condition of the grounds in the weekly log sheet, noting any areas that require attention.

5.3 Mowing Schedule

The main playing field shall be mown twice per week during the growing season (April to October) and once per week during the remainder of the year, weather permitting. The training area shall be mown once per week during the growing season. Mowing shall not take place when the ground is waterlogged or during periods of frost.

5.4 Fertiliser and Top Dressing

- Fertiliser shall be applied to the main playing field in early April and again in early September, using a product approved by the Facilities Lead.
- Top dressing shall be carried out in October, at a rate of approximately 5 tonnes per pitch, to level the surface and encourage root growth.
- All application dates and product names shall be recorded in the Grounds Log Book.

5.5 Aeration

- The main playing field shall be hollow-tine aerated in March and September.
- The training area shall be spiked in May and July.
- Aeration shall be carried out when the soil is moist but not saturated.

5.6 Perimeter Paths

- Perimeter paths shall be swept weekly and any weeds treated with an approved herbicide.
- Loose or broken paving slabs shall be reported to the Facilities Lead and made safe with hazard tape until repaired.

5.7 Trees and Hedges

- Hedges shall be trimmed in August, after the nesting season.
- Trees shall be inspected annually in autumn for dead or dangerous branches. Any such branches shall be removed by a qualified contractor.
- Fallen leaves shall be cleared from paths and the playing surface as required during autumn.

6. Water Quality Testing

6.1 The club has two water features: the ornamental pond near the North Pavilion and the drinking water fountain by the main entrance. The pond is not used for swimming or any other recreational purpose.

6.2 Ornamental Pond

- The pond water shall be tested weekly between April and September, and monthly from October to March.
- The test shall measure pH, ammonia, nitrite, and nitrate levels.
- The results shall be recorded in the Water Quality Log, noting the date, time, and the initials of the person carrying out the test.
- If the pH falls outside the range 6.5 to 8.5, or if ammonia or nitrite levels are above 0.5 mg/l, the Facilities Lead shall be notified and a partial water change shall be carried out.
- The pond pump and filter shall be checked monthly and cleaned as necessary.

6.3 Drinking Water Fountain

- The drinking water fountain shall be inspected weekly for leaks, blockages, and general cleanliness.
- The filter shall be replaced every six months, or sooner if the flow rate reduces noticeably.
- A water sample shall be sent to a UKAS-accredited laboratory annually in June, for microbiological analysis.
- The laboratory certificate shall be filed in the Water Quality Log.

6.4 Emergency Water Supply

In the event of a mains water failure, the club has an emergency water butt located behind the South Pavilion. This supply is for cleaning purposes only and is not suitable for drinking. The butt shall be emptied and cleaned annually in March, and the tap checked for operation.

2.2 The Head Groundskeeper (currently R. Singh) is responsible for the pitch, training area, and all grounds equipment.

- Check that the heating programmer is set for the correct day and time. Reset if the power was interrupted overnight.
- Check that all emergency exit routes are clear and that the emergency lighting test switch is in the normal position.

- Check that the water stopcock is in the open position (only close for winterisation or emergency).
- Check that the toilet flush operates and there is no continuous running water.
- Check that the heater timer is set correctly, if the heater is in use.

**4. GROUNDS MAINTENANCE**

4.1 The Head Groundskeeper is responsible for the overall condition of the playing surfaces, surrounds, and access paths. Daily and weekly tasks are set out below. Seasonal tasks (e.g. end-of-season renovation) are planned separately and communicated by notice on the Grounds Office door and by email.

4.2 **Daily Grounds Checks (playing season, March–October)**

- Walk the perimeter of each pitch before play. Look for glass, litter, dog fouling, or damage to fencing. Remove any debris and log the action in the Grounds Log.
- Check goalposts are secure and padding is in place for all junior matches. Report any loose fixings to the Head Groundskeeper.
- Check that the corner flags are present and not damaged.
- Inspect the run-off areas and spectator lines for trip hazards, especially where the ground has been wet.

4.3 **Weekly Pitch Inspection**

- Carry out a full inspection of each pitch, including the outfield areas. Use the Pitch Inspection Record (Form G-2) and note the following:
  - Grass length (measured with the sward stick, recorded in mm).
  - Any bare patches, divots, or worm casts that need attention.
  - Drainage issues: standing water, soft spots, or silt build-up.
  - Condition of the pitch surrounds, including any damage to the mower access gate.
- The completed form must be handed to the Head Groundskeeper by Friday 12:00. The Head Groundskeeper will decide whether any remedial work is required and will allocate the work accordingly.

4.4 **Mowing**

- Mowing heights are set by the Head Groundskeeper and vary by season. The current settings are displayed on the mower shed noticeboard.
- Do not mow when the grass is wet unless specifically instructed. When mowing, use the agreed pattern (alternate direction each cut) to avoid compaction.
- After mowing, check the underside of the mower for build-up of grass and clean if necessary.
- Report any unusual vibration or cutting irregularities to the Head Groundskeeper before the next use.

4.5 **Fertiliser and Top Dressing**

- Only the Head Groundskeeper or a trained groundsperson may apply fertiliser, top dressing, or other soil amendments.
- All applications must be recorded on the Chemical/Amendment Log (Form G-4), including product name, quantity, area treated, and weather conditions.
- Keep all product safety data sheets in the Grounds Office. The current list of approved products is available from the Clubhouse Manager.

4.6 **Irrigation**

- The automatic irrigation system (N.Pav and S.Pav pitches) is to be tested each Monday morning during the playing season. Check for leaks, blocked heads, and correct timer settings.
- If the system is used manually, the person operating it must remain on site until the cycle is complete.
- Any faults with the irrigation controller should be reported to the Head Groundskeeper and logged in the Defect Log.

---

**5. BOILER AND HEATING SYSTEMS**

5.1 These procedures apply to the clubhouse boiler and the heating systems in N.Pav and S.Pav. Only the Clubhouse Manager or a nominated contractor may carry out work on the boilers themselves. Volunteers must not remove any boiler casing or attempt repairs.

5.2 **Monthly Boiler Check (Clubhouse)**

- Check the pressure gauge. The normal cold reading is between 1.0 and 1.5 bar. If the reading is below 1.0 bar, top up using the filling loop (see 5.4).
- Check that the condensate pipe is not blocked or leaking.
- Check the flue terminal outside for obstructions (e.g. bird nests or debris).
- Listen for unusual noises (kettling, banging) and note any smells of gas or combustion. If gas is smelled, follow the emergency procedure in Section 11.
- Record the check on the Boiler Check Sheet (Form H-2) and file it in the monthly folder.

4.5 Floodlight Array A – North Pitch

Floodlight Array A, with bulb type LED 400W, is equipped with LED lamps. Record status: current. This array was
also inspected on 2025-11-03 by Ashcombe Electrical Services. The array comprises 6 no.
floodlight units (3 no. columns, 2 no. units per column). The columns are located along
the north side of the north pitch, adjacent to the access road.

Column 1 (west) and Column 2 (centre) were inspected from the mobile elevating work
platform. Column 3 (east) was inspected from ground level only due to the ground
conditions around the base; the column base is set on a raised concrete plinth and the
surrounding area was waterlogged following recent rain. The client was advised that a
full access inspection of Column 3 should be arranged when the ground is dry, and that
the plinth drainage should be cleared.

- Column 1: galvanised steel, approximately 12m in height, single cross-arm carrying
  two luminaires. No visible corrosion or damage. Cross-arm and bracket secure.
- Column 2: as Column 1. No visible corrosion or damage. Cross-arm and bracket secure.
- Column 3: galvanised steel, approximately 12m in height, single cross-arm carrying
  two luminaires. Visible from ground level only; no obvious damage or corrosion was
  observed on the lower 3m of the column. The access door was secure and the isolator
  was operated and found to be functional.

The luminaire bodies on Columns 1 and 2 were clean and free of cracks or water ingress.
The lenses were in good condition with no significant discolouration. The isolators at
the column bases were operated and found to be functional. The isolator at Column 2 was
not labelled with the circuit reference; a label was fitted during the inspection and
the client was advised to arrange a permanent engraved label, as with Column 4 on the
south pitch.

The floodlighting was not switched on during the inspection as it was daytime. The
client was advised to carry out a visual check of the luminaire output after dark and
to report any obvious failures or discolouration to the maintenance contractor.

4.6 Earthing and Bonding – Floodlight Array A

The earthing arrangement for Floodlight Array A is TN-S, with the earth terminal at
DB-F/A connected to the main earthing terminal in the North Pavilion. The earth
continuity was verified by testing at the column bases.

- The earth conductor at Column 1 measured 0.07 ohms.
- The earth conductor at Column 2 measured 0.08 ohms.
- The earth conductor at Column 3 was not tested as the isolator could not be isolated
  from the supply without switching off the entire array; the client was advised that
  this test should be completed at the next available maintenance window. The existing
  test certificate for Column 3, dated 2024-06-18, shows an earth continuity reading of
  0.09 ohms.

5. Insulation Resistance Testing

Insulation resistance testing was carried out on the complete floodlighting installation
on 2025-11-03. The supply was isolated and the test was carried out at 500V DC between
each live conductor and earth, and between live conductors.

| Circuit | Test (L-E) | Test (N-E) | Test (L-N) | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DB-F/A – Floodlight Array A (Columns 1-3) | 49.2 MΩ | 48.7 MΩ | 55.1 MΩ | Pass |
| DB-F/B – Floodlight Array B (Columns 4-5) | 52.8 MΩ | 51.4 MΩ | 58.3 MΩ | Pass |

The underground supply cables between the North Pavilion and the column bases were not
visually inspected. No fault was indicated by the insulation resistance testing.

6. RCD Testing

RCD protection is provided at the main distribution board in the North Pavilion. The
following RCDs were tested using a ramp test method:

|---|---|---|---|---|
| DB-F/A RCD 1 | 30 mA | 30 mA | 28 ms | Pass |
| DB-F/B RCD 1 | 30 mA | 30 mA | 31 ms | Pass |
